f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.title: Noche en Blanco Málaga 2026
f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.summary: LNEB es un evento dedicado a la creación cultural en Málaga, que acoge actividades, exposiciones y propuestas artísticas abiertas al público. Esta edición se desarrolla bajo el lema "El futuro se escribe con música", una temática que toma la música como punto de partida para conectar cultura, innovación y participación ciudadana. Para su identidad visual nos hemos inspirado en el movimiento y la vibración del sonido. La propuesta se construye a partir de una tipografía variable y un sistema gráfico vivo, capaz de transformarse y reaccionar a la música. Las formas circulares que componen las letras hacen referencia a los ciclos lunares, conectando visualmente con el imaginario del evento. El sistema visual se expande mediante texturas, deformaciones y animaciones influenciadas por el Op Art, utilizando colores vibrantes y contrastados que refuerzan el carácter del evento. La identidad busca convertirse en una experiencia dinámica e interactiva.

f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.title: TIDAL SCULPTURES ? Iceland
f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.summary: Temporary sand islands in a lagoon on Iceland's east coast, shaped by wind, tides, and rain. Low evening light reveals sculptural ridges, dark textures, and cool blue water.

f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.title: Farseer
f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.summary: Farseer is a financial planning platform built around a spreadsheet interface, giving finance teams a familiar environment with high-performance technology underneath. The brand was built on the same principle. Spreadsheets became the foundation of the identity system, shaped into a visual language that feels lighter, faster, and more human than traditional finance software. When a product changes the way people work, it changes the way they feel about work too. We rebuilt Farseer across verbal identity, visual identity, motion, audio, sub-brands, and a new website.

f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.title: Tiempos inciertos
f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.summary: Visual identity and graphic communication system for Tiempos inciertos (Uncertain Times), the international congress organised by ADACE, the Spanish Association of Contemporary Art Directors, held at the Federico García Lorca Centre in Granada. The event reflects on the present and future of cultural institutions, addressing issues such as governance, collections, sustainability, new technologies and audiences. The graphic proposal builds on ADACE's distinctive yellow underline, a recurring element of its visual identity, expanding it into a vibrant palette inspired by text highlighters. The title Tiempos inciertos is partially obscured by the bands themselves, evoking a present marked by uncertainty, in which everything seems to be under review and in search of balance.

f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.title: OTZ LAB
f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.summary: OTZ LAB is OTEYZA's unisex fragrance collection. We designed the bottle, packaging and visual identity to translate the brand's dialogue between tradition and the avant-garde into perfumery. The bottle pairs the solidity of matte black steel with the fragility of glass, shaped like a test tube to evoke experimentation. A sphere in distinctive colours and textures identifies each fragrance, while the boxes feature compositions inspired by constructivism. A design that reinterprets traditional perfume packaging through structure, material and intention.

f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.title: Piega
f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.summary: PIEGA is a brand direction for a women's label built on the fold. The symbol is a paper pentagon folded into seven pieces. The logo prints itself in reverse, the way wet ink does when you fold a page. Every garment keeps a red the street never sees: a lining, a hem tape, the back of a fold.

f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.title: Our very first painting exhibition
f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.summary: This exhibition explores the meaning of space and place through personal experiences and memories. Each individual shapes their own environment over time, turning it into more than just a physical setting. Everyday moments, like sitting on a chair or drinking water, become part of a deeper emotional landscape.

f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.title: Quantum Security Brand Identity & Pitch Deck
f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.summary: Quantum Deep is a deep-tech company building probabilistic computing hardware for cybersecurity, semiconductors, and post-quantum cryptography. Ahead of a new funding round, they came to us for a brand identity mature enough to match their technology and win the confidence of investors and enterprise customers. We built the full brand foundation: strategy, tone of voice, and a complete visual system with logo, typography, and color. Rather than leaning on generic quantum clichés, we designed a graphic language rooted in probability, photonics, and structured uncertainty. It scales across every touchpoint, from the website and investor pitch decks to 3D product visualization of the chip, brand guidelines, social, and events. A credible, category-defining identity for a B2B deep-tech brand, by Prznt Perfect.

f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.title: Portraits 2023-2026
f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.summary: A collection of hand-drawn digital portrait illustrations inspired by classical engraving, woodcut and traditional pen and ink techniques. The portraits were created for a variety of commercial and editorial projects, including advertising campaigns, corporate portraits, brand identity, packaging design, and commissioned artwork. Combining detailed linework, crosshatching, and a monochrome palette, these illustrations reinterpret the visual language of historical engraving in a contemporary digital medium.

f4b4bb981e:840a78a91f95502a.summary: Da San Chaek Gil is a brand representing the commercial and cultural district of Dasan New Town in Namyangju. Supported by the city government and the Regional Intellectual Property Center under the Korean Intellectual Property Office, FRONT KIT conducted its total branding including the naming which indicates "Da San (area) + San Chaek (stroll) + Chaek (book) + Gil (path)," that are the features of the district. Also, the project encompassed the creation of a comprehensive brand identity, including slogans, storytelling, characters, and application designs that reflect Dasan's vibrant scenery and cultural sentiment. Additionally, intellectual property rights were filed, workshops for merchants were conducted, and the geographic name was officially registered, ensuring a systematic and professional public branding. Da San Chaek Gil will offer a foundation for sustainable growth as an intangible cultural resource for the city.

a4977d3fa4:ce37e8865ea4a22d.title: doublet x POTR Flip Yoshida & Co.’s Standards Into a Bag With Two “A-Sides”
a4977d3fa4:ce37e8865ea4a22d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ce37e8865ea4a22d.summary: Summary POTR and doublet have built a bag with no designated back, inspired by the double A-side singles of the CD eraThe design fuses a mini backpack with a duffel bag, pairing POTR monogram jacquard with a turquoise liningInterchangeable shoulder and hand straps let it be worn crossbody or carried by hand whichever side faces out POTR has joined forces with doublet on a collaborative bag that merges a mini backpack and a duffel into a single, double-sided form. Rather than assigning a front and a back, the piece treats both faces as equals, giving wearers two distinct looks from one silhouette.The concept comes straight from doublet’s design playbook. Masayuki Ino’s Japanese label builds wearable, real-world clothing around humor and surprise, swapping out pieces of familiar staples for unexpected ideas until the result feels just slightly off from the everyday. Here, that thinking lands on the classic Yoshida & Co. bag, borrowing its logic from the double A-side CD single, a release where neither track was treated as the lesser cut.Ino frames the reversible format as a deliberate refusal to settle on one answer. “By not fixing the front and back and reversing the perspective, a new expression is born. The direction changes each time you carry it, and it resonates with your mood and outfit of the day,” he says in a translated statement.Each face gets its own construction. The backpack side is cut from an original jacquard woven with POTR’s monogram and carries a zippered front pocket sized for small essentials like wireless earbuds or lip balm. Flip it around and the duffel side offers a snap-button pocket that doubles as storage: when the backpack face is worn forward, the duffel handles tuck neatly inside it, keeping the profile clean.Color work ties the two halves together. On the pink and khaki versions, the zipper tape is dyed to match the body fabric, so neither side reads as secondary. Open the bag and a turquoise lining, a shade closely tied to POTR’s…

a4977d3fa4:a2dd8d9016f7d95b.title: Inside the World of Anyma: From ‘Genesys’ to ‘ÆDEN’ and His Singapore Debut
a4977d3fa4:a2dd8d9016f7d95b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a2dd8d9016f7d95b.summary: For Anyma, electronic music goes beyond sound. The DJ and producer has built an audiovisual world exploring technology, science fiction and humanity’s relationship with the digital age. With his Genesys trilogy behind him, he’s now expanding that vision through ÆDEN, a new chapter that continues to evolve with each performance.Having taken his productions to the Las Vegas Sphere, Coachella and the Pyramids of Giza, Anyma now makes his Singapore debut during Formula 1 race weekend. The performance marks a return to his club roots, bringing his latest audiovisual world into a different setting after a run of large-scale shows. He takes the stage at MARQUEE Singapore on October 10, 2026.You’re making your Singapore debut right in the middle of race weekend, one of the city’s biggest weekends. What are you looking forward to experiencing while you’re here?Experiencing Singapore and its people properly, as it’s such a beautiful country, as is all of Southeast Asia in general. This region in particular is one I’ve been deeply inspired by in its modern and ancient forms.“Each ÆDEN show is different, with the narrative constantly evolving through new songs and visuals.” Visuals have become a defining part of the Anyma experience. What do you want people to feel when they see them live? I want people to feel an emotion deeper than a party performance. I hope the takeaway feels valuable for the fans and that the thematic narratives of future, past, humanity, and technology ultimately resonate deeper. Of course these are primarily subjective and up to interpretation, but if people leave an ÆDEN show and feel moved in some way, then I’ve achieved my goal.Anyma has grown into an entire world beyond the music. At this point, where does Matteo end and Anyma begin?Creating the Anyma project was really just a combined reflection of who I am and what my passions have been throughout my life. Video games, anime, sci-fi, and fantasy worlds were huge influences on me outside of music,…

a4977d3fa4:855259285fc9a65c.summary: Summary Manual, the New York camera lifestyle label, just opened its first permanent store, Manual Photo Lab, in ChinatownAt 85A Allen Street, the space is designed as a hangout, film lab, equipment store, stocked with cameras, film, books, zines, and moreOpening doors with an exhibition by Leon Xu, founder Malcom Dia says more shows, zine launches, DJ sets, and workshops are in the works New York loves Manual, and Manual loves New York. Now, with the opening of Manual Photo Lab, its first permanent foothold, day-ones and first-timers have a permanent hangout.The 400-square-foot setup in Chinatown was inspired by the mom-and-pop camera stores founder Malcolm Dia grew up around, places that not only specialized in equipment, but served as meeting spots for like-minded artists immersed in their craft. a4977d3fa4:b7c1225b551389f8.title: ‘Roy Lichtenstein: Like New’ Isn’t Your Parents’ Pop Art
a4977d3fa4:b7c1225b551389f8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b7c1225b551389f8.summary: We can’t help it: Roy Lichtenstein is everywhere. From the pixels that make up on-screen images and the thick, brazen linework of even today’s greatest makers to the split-second shot of a tear-stained heroine, his impact is nearly impossible to shake. It’s fast, it’s in your face. But how has his household comics-and-dots shorthand eclipsed a more complex story?“Just because we can recognize something doesn’t mean we fully understand what it is,” said Meg Onli, one of the curators of Roy Lichtenstein: Like New. Opening at the Whitney Museum in New York on October 11, the show brings together over 130 works by the Pop master, including paintings, drawings, collages, prints, and sculptures, created over Lichtenstein’s six-decade career. And while its comic-inspired canvases are plenty, it also unearths lesser-known threads that resemble the artist, both as he saw himself and how his then-radical love for high-low would presciently play to the screen-happy realities of today’s audiences.From the serious, and seriously strange, teachings of Hoyt Sherman at Ohio State University that would later prove formative to Lichtenstein’s outlook on the mark to works created in his last year of life, extending into the 1997 show just upstairs, Like New shines a light on the artist who understood the future of images and a deft appreciation for the eternal making and unmaking of meaning. The introductory, nearly 100-foot recreation of his “Greene Street Mural” (1983), one of four murals recreated by co-curator and artist Alex Da Corte’s studio, sets the tone right.A historic highlight is a literal trip back to Lichtenstein’s New York: a gallery-within-a-gallery reconstruction of the artist’s 1962 debut solo at Leo Castelli gallery. It’s the first reunion of all the works since, down to “Laughing Cat” (1961), originally owned by Andy Warhol. Then lie some of his best-known heroines — “Drowning Girl” (1963), “Crying Girl” (1963), and “Girl in Window (Study for World’s Fair Mural)”…

a4977d3fa4:fa9f9cc446714e82.title: Snoh Aalegra Teases Her Return With New Single “Run Free”
a4977d3fa4:fa9f9cc446714e82.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fa9f9cc446714e82.summary: Summary Snoh Aalegra previewed “Run Free” on October 8th, her first new music since 2023 and a first taste of her upcoming album, 'A Legendary Love.'The track blends classic soul with Prince and 80s pop influences, with a music video directed by Alfred Marroquin.No release date has been announced for "Run Free" or 'A Legendary Love' yet. We just got one step closer to new Snoh Aalegra music. On October 8th, the Swedish singer previewed her track, “Run Free,” on her social media pages, giving fans their first taste of her upcoming project, A Legendary Love. The anticipated album will be Snoh’s first full-length project since 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies. “Run Free” is yet another addition to Snoh’s long list of timeless ballads, and her first new music since 2023, with this song particularly fitting as the soundtrack to the end of a coming-of-age film. The Prince and 80s pop influence is apparent in the song’s exquisite production, as in typical Snoh Aalegra fashion, she fuses classic soul with modern textures, creating a cinematic, soulful soundscape of love, heartbreak, and introspection. In the song’s grainy, minimalistic music video directed by Alfred Marroquin, Snoh sings “Trouble before me, I can’t see. My love is forever, here I see / Falling in and out of my mind, don’t ever see it through / I know it won’t change anything, but I wanted to / I used to see, I used to see two hearts run free,” as she cruises through winding, desolate, tree-lined streets in the back of a vintage BMW. With “Run Free” being her first song since 2023, fans are patiently waiting, finding a pixelated album cover and teasers on her website, alegendarylove.com. The official release date for “Run Free” and A Legendary Love has not been announced yet. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:420ac6cdd91bd37d.title: Bangkok Watch Week 2026 Proves There's More to Watch Culture Than Collecting
a4977d3fa4:420ac6cdd91bd37d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:420ac6cdd91bd37d.summary: Bangkok has long been home to some of the world's most passionate watch collectors. Now, it's building an international stage to match. The second edition of Siam Paragon Bangkok Watch Week, held from September 22 to 27, 2026, made a compelling case for the Thai capital's growing influence on the global horological calendar. Drawing more than 40,000 visitors across six days, the event brought the world of fine watchmaking into sharper focus, positioning Bangkok as a meeting place for luxury, craftsmanship and a thriving collecting culture.Hosted by Siam Piwat at Siam Paragon, this year's edition brought together more than 45 established watch maisons and independent creators, with returning names such as Cartier and Vacheron Constantin joined by newcomers including MB&F and Ressence. More than 200 novelties shared the spotlight alongside the Southeast Asian debut of the Fondation de la Haute Horlogerie (FHH). Yet beyond its expanding roster and exclusive presentations, Bangkok Watch Week's defining ambition lay in bringing the industry and its audiences closer together.Unlike the closed-door formats of traditional European watch fairs, Siam Piwat intentionally prioritized community-building and inclusivity over a standard exhibition layout. Caroline Murphy, President of Strategic Project Development at Siam Piwat, notes that the company approaches retail fundamentally differently from traditional landlords. "We didn't want to do another commercial event," Murphy explains. Serving as a direct evolution of Florence Knoll’s iconic 1961 credenzas, the collection honors the rigorous steel, veneer, and marble construction logic of the original pieces while introducing entirely new forms and proportions. The collection falls into a category described by Knoll Creative Director Jonathan Olivares as "adaptive reuse," extending classic architectural visions to encourage more fluid ways of living and working.The resulting pieces shift storage from a purely practical necessity into an architectural backdrop for books, objects and personal artifacts. Tall open shelving extends the system vertically, creating a stronger spatial presence while also offering opportunities to subtly divide a room, while a dedicated bar cabinet turns storage into a focal point for entertaining.Coffee, side and console tables broaden the collection further, incorporating concealed drawers that bring everyday organization into lower, more informal furniture typologies. Visually, the pieces retain the clean geometry and rigor associated with Florence Knoll’s original credenzas, but Chermayeff introduces a more expressive character through altered proportions and a newly energized palette, including Dark Red Ultra, Dark Python and Iris lacquer finishes.That balance between historical continuity and contemporary flexibility separates Chermayeff Storage from a conventional Knoll reissue. a4977d3fa4:330516b4fd09faf1.title: Alpha Industries Just Blacked Out the MA-1, B-15 and CWU-45 for Its “Triple Black Pack”
a4977d3fa4:330516b4fd09faf1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:330516b4fd09faf1.summary: Summary Alpha Industries applies sneaker culture’s “triple black” formula to three of its most recognizable flight jacketsShell, lining and branding tag all go black, removing the contrast linings long tied to the label’s outerwearA campaign set inside a fictional design lab follows the jackets from raw material to finished garment to wearer Alpha Industries has unveiled the Triple Black Pack for FW26, reworking the MA-1 Heritage, B-15 Intermediate Flight Jacket and CWU-45 Heritage in black from the outer shell through to the lining and tag. The result is a trio of the brand’s core flight jackets stripped of every contrasting element.The concept comes from footwear. In sneaker circles, “triple black” describes a shoe where the upper, midsole and outsole all share the same black finish. Alpha Industries maps that three-part formula directly onto its jackets, with the shell, the lining and the tag standing in for those three zones.The lining is where the change lands hardest. Contrast linings have been a defining feature of Alpha’s flight jackets for decades, none more recognizable than the bright orange inside the MA-1. Here, that pop of color is gone entirely. With black running through every layer, the jackets now present a single, unbroken tone, so the look stays consistent whether the zip is done up or the front hangs open.The silhouettes themselves remain familiar. The MA-1 Heritage, B-15 Intermediate Flight Jacket and CWU-45 Heritage each keep the shapes Alpha fans already know, with the all-black treatment serving as the sole transformation. That restraint keeps the focus on color as the design statement, letting the blacked-out finish do the work.The Alpha Industries Triple Black Pack is available now online, at selected retailers and the Alpha Industries Store in Frankfurt am Main. a4977d3fa4:d64ba1b1eeec4540.summary: The Roots of AuthenticityJapanese hip-hop’s early history was anchored in Tokyo, where a generation captivated by rap’s refined style watched as the genre entered its first domestic boom. By the mid-1990s, tracks like “DA.YO.NE” pushed hip-hop into the mainstream, but beneath the surface, a divide emerged between commercial "pop" rap and the underground. While the media turned "check it out" into a meme, the underground scene rejected commercialism, with artists quietly sharpening their skills through intense competition.The genba (frontline) of this movement was Shibuya’s Club CAVE, where the event “A BAOA QU” became a sanctuary for individuals who shared a "fly" conviction – a space where figures from music and fashion searched for like-minded peers. Here, the blueprint for NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND (NMU) began to form through organic connections rather than a calculated plan to start a group.Formation and the "Reality" of the SceneThe future members were already fixtures in the Shibuya and Harajuku scenes: MACKA-CHIN and XBS were high school classmates; GORE-TEX and S-WORD worked in Shibuya; while SUIKEN and DABO ran events in Nishi-Azabu. Their bond deepened naturally through the shops and clubs they frequented. When they were offered a monthly residency at CAVE, the parties quickly became legendary.In an era when recording equipment was scarce, rappers typically performed original lyrics over imported US 12-inch instrumentals — a practice in which one’s taste was judged by their choice of beat. As these vibrant parties drew staff from iconic record shops like Manhattan Records and CISCO, a collective of roughly 30 people solidified under the loose banner of "about NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND." This momentum caught the eye of Kazuteru Maekawa of Lexington Co., Ltd., who proposed a collaboration. Despite a lingering aversion to "selling out," those who remained committed - while others left for conventional jobs - formed the core of NMU.The Shibuya Udagawa…

a4977d3fa4:3c945e70d0a364d2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3c945e70d0a364d2.summary: Summary Anthony Vaccarello is officially exiting Saint Laurent after 10 years as Creative DirectorThe Belgian designer transformed the French house into a high-glamour powerhouse with sales peaking at 3.3 billion eurosParent company Kering announced it will reveal new creative leadership for the brand soon Saint Laurent and parent company Kering have officially confirmed the departure of Creative Director Anthony Vaccarello after a decade leading the house. The Belgian designer's dramatic September runway presentation in Paris served as his final collection for the luxury brand.Vaccarello took the creative reins in 2016 following Hedi Slimane, establishing a distinct visual language anchored in high-octane glamour, sharp tailoring, and sensual eveningwear presented against the backdrop of the Eiffel Tower. During his ten-year tenure, Saint Laurent’s annual revenues nearly tripled to a peak of €3.3 billion EUR, driven by popular everyday leather goods, sharp footwear, and statement outerwear alongside runway showpieces. Beyond fashion, Vaccarello expanded the brand’s cultural influence in 2023 with the launch of Saint Laurent Productions, backing films by directors including Pedro Almodóvar and David Cronenberg. On Vaccarello's departure, Luca de Meo, CEO of Kering said, "I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Anthony for his contribution to Saint Laurent over the past 10 years. Through his creative vision and exacting standards, he has contributed to strengthening the enduring influence of one of France's greatest couture houses, as we embark on a new chapter in its history."His exit comes as Kering undergoes a broader strategic turnaround under new Chief Executive Luca De Meo and Saint Laurent CEO Cédric Charbit. Moving forward, the house aims to reassert its authority beyond eveningwear by reinforcing its daywear, menswear, and high-end leather goods offerings. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:5fc086fde6ca8e57.summary: Summary RIMOWA introduces two pigment-inspired seasonal hues, Umber and Ultramarine, across its Essential and Groove collectionsEssential suitcases are tonally matched from shell to wheel housing and pair a compression system with a dual-zone interiorA new Groove Mini Shopping Bag in Italian calfskin leads a leather and accessories edit split between the two colors RIMOWA has added Umber and Ultramarine to its Essential and Groove collections, two seasonal hues named after pigments that painters have worked with for centuries. Fronted by English actor Joe Alwyn, the release covers polycarbonate luggage, calfskin bags and travel accessories, with each piece finished in a single tone from top to bottom.The palette begins with the pigments themselves. Umber, an earthy brown, takes its name from umbra, the Latin word for shadow, and is frequently used to lay down the base coat of a painting. Ultramarine comes from lapis lazuli, a costly blue that artists have prized since the Renaissance. On the luggage, the pair plays as a study in contrast: Umber gives off a warm, grounded glow, while Ultramarine reads deep and saturated.On the Essential range, the color runs through every component. The polycarbonate shell is matched to the handle, zipper, logo badge and wheel housing, so no contrasting hardware interrupts the monochrome finish. RIMOWA backs that up with its signature running gear: a telescopic handle that extends without fixed stops, the Multiwheel system and TSA-approved locks, plus a complimentary leather address tag. Sizing spans the Cabin through to the Trunk Plus, though not every format comes in both shades, as the Check-In M is offered only in Ultramarine and the Check-In L only in Umber.Open the case and the interior divides into two zones. One side holds a fully zipped compartment and a large mesh pocket, while the other houses RIMOWA’s adjustable Flex Divider. A built-in compression system lets travelers fit more in without sacrificing order, and the…

a4977d3fa4:8ad1692c24e5c5df.title: "The 90s: Art and Fashion" Exhibition Opens, Looking Back at the Frenzy of 1990s British Culture
a4977d3fa4:8ad1692c24e5c5df.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8ad1692c24e5c5df.summary: "The 90s: Art and Fashion," the first major exhibition to explore the rapid development and excitement of art, photography, and fashion in 1990s Britain, has opened at London's national gallery, Tate Britain. Co-curated by Edward Enninful, known as the former editor-in-chief of British Vogue, the exhibition re-examines a groundbreaking era that fundamentally rewrote the UK's cultural identity through over 100 works including paintings, sculptures, photography, and garments. It runs from Thursday, October 8, 2026, to Sunday, February 14, 2027.The new generation that emerged following the recession of the 1980s put forward a DIY ethos and a gritty reality that rejected perfection. The exhibition showcases "anti-fashion" grunge-style photography by Corinne Day and Juergen Teller, who were active in magazines like i-D and Dazed and Confused, as well as iconic visuals capturing Kate Moss. It also features a host of electric photos and videos tracking the scenes of acid house, hip-hop, drum and bass, and rave culture, exemplified by Manchester's legendary club the Haçienda and London's Bagley's.Furthermore, the show brings together works by the Young British Artists (YBAs) like Tracey Emin and Damien Hirst, who drove the conceptual and shocking art scene of the time, alongside sensational dress ensembles created by Alexander McQueen and Hussein Chalayan, who brilliantly shattered the boundaries between fashion and art. The exhibition also sheds light on the issues of race, class, and diversity that lay beneath the frenzy of "Cool Britannia," making for a spectacular experience that unpacks the energy and challenges of late-20th-century Britain from multiple angles.The 90s: Art and FashionDates: Thursday, October 8, 2026 – Sunday, February 14, 2027Venue: Tate BritainAddress: Millbank, London SW1P 4RG, UKHours: 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m. (Open daily)Official Website View this post on InstagramA post shared by HYPEBEAST (@hypebeast) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:55a7939cebf09d5f.title: Las Vegas Aces' A'ja Wilson Wins Historic Fifth WNBA MVP Award
a4977d3fa4:55a7939cebf09d5f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:55a7939cebf09d5f.summary: Summary Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson has won her fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award for the 2026 seasonThe victory marks the first time in WNBA history a player has captured three consecutive MVP honorsWilson declined a traditional pregame presentation ceremony ahead of Game 3 to remain focused on the team's playoff run Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson has officially secured her historic fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player award for the 2026 season. The milestone achievement makes Wilson the first player in league history to capture three consecutive MVP honors.Wilson dominated the voting, receiving 65 out of 74 first-place votes to finish ahead of Lynx rookie guard Olivia Miles and Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell. Across 41 regular-season games, she became the first WNBA player to average at least 25 points while shooting 50 percent from the floor and 40 percent from three-point range. Her 26.2 points per game led the league alongside top marks in blocks, Player Efficiency Rating, and Win Shares.The victory aligns Wilson with five-time MVP winners across professional sports history, joining NBA legends Michael Jordan and Bill Russell. Despite the recognition, Wilson elected to forgo a center-court pregame trophy presentation ahead of Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries, choosing instead to focus on warming up with her teammates. a4977d3fa4:0447d2fec82843d8.title: How WHATMORE Turned a Group Chat into New York’s Next Great Music Movement
a4977d3fa4:0447d2fec82843d8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:0447d2fec82843d8.summary: Behind the scenes of Hypebeast’s September Digital Cover with WHATMORE, our latest Diaries series features the boundary-pushing New York collective—composed of Cisco Swank, Elijah Judah, Jackson August, Yoshi T., and Sebastiano ($eb)—the energy is as raw, electric, and effortlessly laid-back as their music. Originating from their high school days at LaGuardia High, the group's real-life bond and yearslong group chat have finally manifested into live festival stages and a defining digital feature. Pulling up to the venue with Toyota's all-electric C-HR parked outside, the crew blended modern city mobility with their distinct streetwear aesthetic before stepping inside to kick off a night centered around pure sound, community, and forward-thinking energy.Before the venue doors opened and lights went low, the group kept things grounded backstage. Between playing hand after hand of card games on plush couches surrounded by lush indoor greenery and sharing quick bites, the atmosphere felt like a hangout at a home studio rather than a high-profile cover shoot. "I always make sure my homies eat before they get to do shows and stuff," Elijah Judah shared softly, capturing the quiet loyalty that holds the quintet together. That sense of unspoken trust extends into their prep—whether they are casually running through beats on a laptop, going over vocals, or joking around before soundcheck.When it was time to run sound, the quiet pre-show ritual quickly shifted into focused performance mode. Taking the stage in a light-filled warehouse surrounded by exposed brick and vintage monitors, WHATMORE dialed in every technical detail. Jackson August plugged into his headset mic with an easy confidence, leaning over the mic to declare, "I'm listening to a banger right now... You can't hear it, but this shit is fire." a4977d3fa4:323582bb0405e2a1.title: Gen Z Art Collectors Are the Biggest Spenders
a4977d3fa4:323582bb0405e2a1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:323582bb0405e2a1.summary: Summary Art Basel and UBS have released the fifth edition of Survey of Global Collecting for 2026Major findings include lofty spending habits for Gen Z collectors, whose average expenditure is twice that of millennials and boomersThe study also shows the uptick in social media, apps, and AI tools when it comes to discovery and research, with a "broadly positive" attitude towards the development of new technologies in the collecting space Gen Z collectors are outspending their parents and grandparents nearly twofold, studies by Arts Economics show. Art Basel and UBS have released the 2026 Survey of Global Collecting, and the latest report arrives with some major findings on the “who” and “how” abuzz in the art market.The young “omnivore collectors,” as Art Basel described Gen Z collectors last year, have prevailed, outspending their generational peers in “virtually every segment,” with the group’s average expenditure in the first half of 2026 alone surpassing the full-year 2025 figure.Among the only 1% of collectors who bought an over-$1 million USD work in 2025, almost half of them were Gen Z, with promising stats pointing to a similar amount in 2026. Lower-priced works, across ages, attracted the most noise, with 77% of high net-worth individuals (HNWI) with an overall sub-$50,000 spending on fine art and 84% under $100,000 in 2026 so far.As seen in recent years, younger collectors, alongside women of all age groups, were more open to discovery -- 56% of Gen Z purchased work by an unfamiliar artist versus 36% of boomers, and 49% of women versus 43% of men.The youngest collectors, perhaps surprisingly, were also some of the most private. This year’s survey debuted a new study on how collectors opted to share their pieces. 39% of Gen Z kept their collection to in-person viewings with close family, friends, and households, nearly twice that of any other generation. They’re also keeping their online collections locked down, with Gen Z leading the pack when it comes…

a4977d3fa4:77a773768f935f19.title: Enio Arroyo Gomez’s 'Ladrón' Finds a Home in Queens
a4977d3fa4:77a773768f935f19.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:77a773768f935f19.summary: Summary Costa Rican artist Enio Arroyo Gomez’s 'Ladrón de casas' takes over an Astoria billboard as part of SaveArtSpace’s Looking In public art initiative.Blending childlike imagination with themes of migration, displacement and belonging, the work explores our complicated relationship with home. Words by Matilda BerkeAbove an unassuming triangular parking lot in Astoria, Queens, the newest installation in SaveArtSpace’s public art initiative Looking In features Costa Rican painter and sculptor Enio Arroyo Gomez’s Ladrón de casas (2018): a depiction of a chimerical bug-eyed figure which, even as he flees with a townhouse in his hand, turns back to face the viewer while he gestures at his prize. At first glance, the image simply suggests the accessible, relatable product of a fanciful imagination. But upon closer inspection, the creature’s posture and expression—coupled with its slightly off-kilter placement in its surreal, tightly framed setting—make it harder to pin down. Curator and award-winning artist Jessica Alazraki selected this work from Gomez’s Bestiario series, which hybridizes medieval bestiaries (encyclopedic compendia of real and imagined animals) with broader themes and techniques in the artist’s own practice as well as his day job as a children’s art teacher.Gomez, who architects his school’s classrooms to promote freeform experimentation and maximize his students’ creativity, similarly designs his curriculum around the kind of automatic drawing that guides his own work. Like his deceptively complex Ladrón, his art is not as naïve as it initially appears. (As Meyer Schapiro writes in “On Some Problems in the Semiotics of Visual Art: Field and Vehicle in Image-Signs,” “the figure appears anomalous, displaced, even spiritually strained… the self-constrained posture and other elements of the image work to reinforce an expression of the brooding and withdrawn. The tendency to favor an off-center position has been noticed in the drawings of emotionally…

a4977d3fa4:06a5f07442b3dbcc.title: Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Burna Boy, and More Are Taking Over the Radio in 'Grand Theft Auto VI'
a4977d3fa4:06a5f07442b3dbcc.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:06a5f07442b3dbcc.summary: Music has always played a major role in the Grand Theft Auto universe. Whether it's cruising through Los Santos with Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg on the radio or tuning into the sounds of '80s Miami on Vice City's iconic Flash FM, Rockstar Games has made its in-game radio stations just as memorable as the worlds players explore. And for Grand Theft Auto VI, it's pulling out all the stops.Rockstar Games has officially unveiled six of the radio stations coming to GTA VI, enlisting a stacked lineup of artists and cultural figures to serve as their hosts. Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Burna Boy, Morgan Wallen, Robyn, Trick Daddy, Trina, and even Slayer's Kerry King and Tom Araya are among the names lending their voices to the game's fictional airwaves.Each station offers its own distinct sound, reflecting the musical landscape of Leonida, the game's fictional take on Florida. Bad Bunny and RaiNao are taking over Cocoteo FM, a station dedicated to Latin music spanning bachata, merengue, dembow, and reggaeton. Meanwhile, Burna Boy and electronic producer Palms Trax will host AfroBank FM, spotlighting everything from African classics and deep cuts to contemporary amapiano and 3-step.For Burna Boy, the opportunity marks a full-circle moment in his relationship with the franchise. Having previously appeared on GTA V's iFruit Radio with "Killin Dem" and contributed "Gettin' Money" to GTA Online's Cayo Perico update, the Nigerian superstar is now getting a station of his own."I've been playing GTA since way before my music ever made it into the game, so this one is personal," Burna Boy tells Hypebeast exclusively. "Then 'Killin Dem' got on iFruit Radio, we did 'Gettin' Money' for Cayo Perico, and now I have my own station in GTA VI. That whole journey is crazy to me.""AfroBank FM is special because it gives us a space to bring our sound, our energy and our culture into a world I've been part of as a player for years," he continues. "GTA has always understood that the music is part of…

a4977d3fa4:7b97e6b346ceee0d.title: Destinee Ross-Sutton on Why the Wrong Gallery Is Worse Than No Gallery
a4977d3fa4:7b97e6b346ceee0d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7b97e6b346ceee0d.summary: Summary 'State of Art' is a new HypeArt series inviting artists, curators, collectors and other leading voices to weigh in on the ideas, debates and cultural shifts shaping contemporary art. Through intimate questions and personal recommendations, the series offers a closer look at what is exciting the art world, what needs to change and where things may be heading next. For artists today, visibility no longer depends on being discovered by a gallery. Social media has collapsed many of the barriers that once separated artists from collectors, curators and audiences, while direct sales and self-organized exhibitions have made it increasingly possible to build a career outside the traditional gallery system.For Destinee Ross-Sutton, that does not mean galleries have become obsolete. It means they have to prove their value. “I don’t think every artist needs a gallery,” the Harlem-born curator and founder of Ross-Sutton Gallery tells Hypeart. “But I do know the right gallery can be an essential partner.”In the latest edition of 'State of Art,' Ross-Sutton considers what representation actually means in 2026, from the shifting power dynamic between artists and dealers to the increasingly contested 50-percent gallery commission.Social media, she argues, has fundamentally changed the entire landscape. Artists can now introduce their work to thousands of people without waiting for a dealer, critic or curator to grant them access. They can watch their own markets develop in real time, identify collectors and, at a rapid fire pace, sell work directly."Galleries are no longer really the gatekeepers" – Destinee Ross-SuttonBut visibility, she stresses, should not be confused with longevity. A serious career requires an infrastructure that extends far beyond finding a buyer. At its best, a gallery provides strategy, trusted relationships, institutional access and an understanding of how decisions made today might affect an artist five or ten years down their career.“A good…

a4977d3fa4:181e922b9d2b78dd.title: Wren Builds the Vessel Watch Around a Double-Faceted Sapphire Crystal
a4977d3fa4:181e922b9d2b78dd.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:181e922b9d2b78dd.summary: Summary Wren introduced the Vessel, a futuristic integrated-bracelet 904L steel watch.It features a world-first sapphire crystal with mirrored top-and-bottom curved facets.Limited to 300 pieces total, prices start at $2,900 USD. Wren is moving beyond the dive-watch category with The Vessel, a new integrated-bracelet sports watch that marks a significant expansion of the young New York independent’s design language.Founded in 2024 and previously known for limited-run divers such as the Diver 38 Mad and Diver One Abyss, Wren approached the Vessel with a deliberately forward-looking brief: create a sports watch that feels inspired by 2075 rather than 1975. Founder Craig Karger brought in British watch designer Max Resnick - whose recent work includes Anoma and VPC - to develop the project, marking the first time Wren has collaborated with an outside designer. After roughly two years of development, the resulting 39mm cushion-shaped, stainless-steel case moves away from familiar integrated-bracelet templates while building the entire architecture around one defining component: its unusually complex sapphire crystal.Rather than treating faceted sapphire as a decorative finishing touch, the Vessel uses a crystal with matching curved facets cut into both its exterior and underside, with the internal surface acting as a precise negative of the geometry above. According to Wren, this mirrored construction is intended to prevent the dial distortion that can occur when a faceted outer crystal is paired with a flat or conventionally domed underside.Developing it proved particularly challenging: an early prototype batch yielded only five usable crystals out of 100 before Wren eventually partnered with a specialist sapphire-case manufacturer capable of producing the required form. The same bespoke approach extends to the bracelet, which features Wren’s own quick-release mechanism and a micro-adjustment system integrated directly into the links rather than the clasp. Two dial…

a4977d3fa4:8920dd9401ff02f1.summary: Summary NOMOS updates two Metro models with new Ice Blue metallic dials.The 37mm Date Power Reserve debuts the hand-wound DUW 4701 calibre.The 40.5mm neomatik 41 Update pairs automatic winding with NOMOS’ ring-date display. NOMOS is cooling down its Metro collection with two new “Ice Blue” references, translating the line’s urban design language into a pale metallic finish inspired by contemporary glass-and-steel architecture.Designed by Berlin-based product designer Mark Braun, Metro has balanced precision, negative space and playful color since its introduction in 2014, when the original Metro Date Power Reserve became the first NOMOS watch equipped with the manufacture’s proprietary swing system escapement. The new Metro Date Power Reserve Ice Blue and Metro neomatik 41 Update Ice Blue retain those familiar codes while shifting the palette toward light blue, teal and muted grey, with galvanized dials that move from cool blue to nearly white depending on the surrounding light.The Metro Date Power Reserve Ice Blue, reference 1121, comes in a compact 37mm stainless-steel case measuring just 8mm thick, pairing its metallic dial with blue and white dot indexes, grey minute numerals and a tri-color power reserve indicator rendered in white, light blue and teal. More significantly, it debuts the new hand-wound DUW 4701, replacing the DUW 4401 used by the original 2014 model. The 2.8mm-thick in-house movement delivers a 52-hour power reserve and patented quick-set date, while its sapphire caseback reveals a skeletonized balance cock, NOMOS perlage, gold engravings and sunburst decoration surrounding the swing system.The larger Metro neomatik 41 Update Ice Blue, reference 1166, measures 40.5mm across and 9.1mm thick, using the automatic DUW 6101 with a 48-hour reserve. Its signature ring-date display places the entire month around the dial perimeter, with two teal markers framing the current date, while a woven waterproof grey textile strap reinforces the cooler, more…

a4977d3fa4:2d07c92fc84479ac.title: everyone Takes Over BELOWGROUND With Hong Kong-Exclusive Releases
a4977d3fa4:2d07c92fc84479ac.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2d07c92fc84479ac.summary: Summary Tokyo-based label everyone makes its Hong Kong debut at BELOWGROUND from October 9 - 13.The pop-up features Hong Kong-exclusive apparel, signature essentials and collaborations with A.PRESSE, adidas Originals and othersPostmodern furniture by Ettore Sottsass and Shiro Kuramata completes the space. Tokyo-based streetwear label everyone, founded by Ryo Miyoshi, is making its official Hong Kong debut with a temporary brick-and-mortar space at BELOWGROUND. Running from October 9 - 13, 2026, the pop-up follows a milestone year for the brand that included opening a new flagship in Maebashi and a Tadao Ando-designed atelier in Seijo.Celebrated for its understated aesthetic and precise fabrications, everyone’s temporary retail store brings a curated selection of its signature Fall 2026 Collection alongside exclusive collaborative works. Highlights include a new Nylon Silk drizzler jacket created specifically for the Hong Kong release, city-exclusive graphics like the ESS Tee and Vincent Logo LS Tee, Loro Piana fabric easy slacks, and select pieces from A.PRESSE for everyone.The temporary space also serves as an immersive showcase of Miyoshi's passion for design, art and collaborative culture. Visitors can browse high-profile joint releases - including footwear and apparel with adidas Originals, SUICOKE, Erik Schedin, and Tomo Nariai - while enjoying an environment curated with iconic postmodern furniture. Key interior display pieces include Ettore Sottsass’s Carlton room divider and Shiro Kuramata’s Progetti Compiuti chest of drawers for Cappellini.Located at Shop B57-B58 in the basement of Landmark Atrium, Central, the everyone brick-and-mortar pop-up welcomes guests daily from 10:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. throughout its five-day run.everyone Temporary Brick-and-MortarShop B57-B58, BELOWGROUNDB1/F, Landmark Atrium15 Queen’s Road Central, Hong Kong Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:b2be7039ca6759da.title: MAAP Brings Its LaB Retail Concept to London for the First Time
a4977d3fa4:b2be7039ca6759da.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b2be7039ca6759da.summary: Summary MAAP opens its first UK LaB concept store in London's Soho district.Designed by Clare Cousins Architects, the space blends cycling-inspired industrial details with historic architectural references.The flagship officially launches October 10, hosting community rides and events. Melbourne-based cycling apparel brand MAAP has opened its first UK flagship in London's Soho district, marking the latest expansion of its Life around Bikes (LaB) retail concept.Located at 29 Great Pulteney Street, the 140-square-meter space becomes MAAP's 11th store worldwide, joining existing locations in cities including Melbourne, Berlin, Sydney and Los Angeles. First introduced in Melbourne in 2022, the LaB concept extends beyond conventional retail, positioning each location as a cultural and social hub for local cycling communities. Alongside the brand's performance-driven apparel and lifestyle offerings, the London outpost is designed to host community rides, talks and activations, bringing together cycling, contemporary design and the creative energy of its surrounding neighborhood.Designed in partnership with Clare Cousins Architects, the store’s interior seamlessly merges MAAP’s modern aesthetic with nods to Soho’s heritage and cycling culture. Features include a cobbled stone floor referencing both local streets and classic one-day bike races, complemented by industrial stainless steel, aluminum, vivid green accents, and a curved steel wall that reflects movement like a peloton. Following a soft launch in early September, MAAP LaB London officially opens on October 10, 2026, marked by a week of ride-outs, celebratory events, and in-store activations. a4977d3fa4:f61d0ea443800362.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f61d0ea443800362.summary: Plaster has joined forces with London-based artist Soldier, real name Leonard Iheagwam, to bring his latest set of artwork to life at their collaborative exhibition titled "Military Abstractions”.Launching ahead of Frieze London, Soldier’s exhibition will span across the first two floors of Plaster’s HQ in Soho. The exhibit acts as an extension of Plaster's ongoing mission of platforming young artists and bridging the gap between the art community through in-person events. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Soldier has been building himself as one of the most exciting voices growing within the London art scene.Frequently reflecting on his personal experience, Soldier pulls inspiration from Lagos' skateboarding scene, church and Military surplus, which materialize through various visual signatures. “Military Abstractions” explores Soldier’s staple motifs, including camouflage and toy soldiers, which act as a visual portrayal of geopolitical and military power, researching deeper into the consequences of war and foreign influence on countries that have experienced colonization. Camouflage is reclaimed from its original connotations and transformed through collages central to Soldier’s personal perspective and artistic practice.Four out of the six new large-scale artworks set to be on display will be available for sale alongside signed posters and limited-edition T-shirts. An exclusive release of 50 original editions are also scheduled for online purchase via a registration-only drop, set to launch simultaneously with the private viewing.It's an exciting collaboration between Plaster and Soldier that will bring together the art world, celebrating young artists expanding out of London.Check out the imagery in the gallery above including both Plaster and Soldier’s Instagrams for updates. a4977d3fa4:b686cf8436ed551a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b686cf8436ed551a.summary: Summary New Balance Japan has signed a Diamond Partner agreement to serve as the official supplier for Samurai JapanThe brand created redesigned home and visitor uniforms debuting at the RAGZAS Asia Professional Baseball Championship 2026The new uniforms and apparel line drop October 20 via New Balance official storefronts New Balance Japan has signed a landmark Diamond Partner agreement with NPB Enterprises Co., Ltd., officially becoming the supplier for Samurai Japan. The partnership equips all of the baseball national team representatives across every age bracket—from the U-12 youth squads to the top national team—with uniforms, performance apparel, footwear, and equipment.Marking the next evolution in New Balance's global baseball expansion, the brand collaborated directly with Samurai Japan to engineer redesigned home and visitor kits from scratch. The home game uniform introduces a new central stripe featuring safflower red layered over traditional Japanese indigo (kachi-iro), symbolizing the spirit of Bushido. For visitor games, the kit adopts a calm, dignified "wabi-sabi" gray palette that mirrors New Balance's signature brand colorway.The collection also introduces a newly developed "SJ" monogram logo displayed across the baseball caps, designed to connect traditional sports heritage with everyday lifestyle wear. Outside of elite competition, New Balance and Samurai Japan will actively collaborate on grassroots outreach programs aimed at expanding youth participation and growing baseball culture across Japan.The new Samurai Japan uniforms and baseball caps launch on October 20, 2026, via the official New Balance online store and select retail locations. a4977d3fa4:8e27a1328753018c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8e27a1328753018c.summary: Summary Steven Spielberg has taken on the task of overseeing the entire 'Transformers' franchise for Paramount PicturesThe filmmaker will executive produce and guide creative direction for 'Transformers 8' alongside Lorenzo di BonaventuraParamount has officially cancelled the previously teased 'Transformers' and 'G.I. Joe' crossover project Paramount Pictures has appointed Steven Spielberg to helm creative direction for the entire Transformers franchise. The decision arrives as development begins on an eighth live-action feature based on the Hasbro IP.Working alongside longtime producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura, Spielberg will executive produce Transformers 8 while taking hands-on control of the overarching creative direction for the property. The partnership aims to recapture the tone of the earlier Transformers entries, which Spielberg helped shape during the franchise's inception. The upcoming eighth film is being written by Jason Fuchs and will be set in the modern day, though plot details and a director remain unannounced.Additionally, Paramount confirmed that former franchise star Shia LaBeouf will not return for the new installment. The studio also revealed that the previously teased Transformers and G.I. Joe crossover film has been officially shelved, allowing both properties to develop as independent franchises. d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.title: Relative Development and the Intelligence Divide: Human Capital, Technology Diffusion, and AI
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.author: Jonathan R. W. Temple
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help poorer countries catch up? This paper argues that the answer depends less on access to AI than on the capacity to use new knowledge productively. We show that countries have narrowed gaps in capital and schooling more readily than gaps in productivity. Technology can diffuse widely without producing productivity convergence. Measured human capital explains only a modest share of productivity differences in levels, but is associated with sharply different mobility regimes. The estimated transition processes imply an expected time to exit the lowest-productivity state of about 65 years for economies below the estimated human-capital threshold, compared with about 25 years for those above it. This reconciles development accounting with the view of human capital as absorptive capacity. If AI mainly augments skilled workers and capable firms, it may reinforce existing gaps. If it lowers the costs of learning, adaptation, and implementation in weaker-capability economies, it could instead promote convergence. The Intelligence Divide is therefore not simply about access to AI, but about the capacity to turn knowledge into productivity.

fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.title: Growth in Chains: EU Value Chain Productivity and its Slowdown
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.author: Lähdemäki, Sakari
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.summary: Abstract We study Europe’s post-2008 productivity slowdown using novel total factor productivity (TFP) measures that follow production beyond individual industries in global value chains (GVCs). We collect a newset of stylized facts: (1) the slowdown is broad-based, with productivity growth weakening both in final-producer industries and in upstream industries; (2) the staggered entry into force of bilateral investment treaties with China is followed by higher value-chain TFP and greater business-intangible investment; while (3) the gains associated with technology intangibles are weak. We use these facts to discipline a stylized two-region general-equilibrium model with business capabilities, technology-related knowledge, and cross-border knowledge spillovers. The calibration supports a two-stage interpretation of Europe’s experience: (1) sizeable initial integration gains because accumulated business capabilities convert market access into productivity, and (2) later losses when technology improvements are converted into productivity more effectively elsewhere.

fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.title: What Does Venture Capital Actually Finance ? Scale and Structure around the World
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.author: Mauro, Paolo
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.summary: Venture capital is widely viewed as financing knowledge-intensive, R&D-driven startups, but owing to data constraints, this view has been based largely on high-income economies. By taking a global perspective, this paper documents that what venture capital finances differs systematically across economies, varying with institutional and business conditions rather than following a single model. Using a new cross-country dataset that harmonizes firm-level venture capital records with equity issuance data for more than 150 economies, the data shows that VC markets differ across countries not only in scale but in kind. Outside high-income countries, rather than being concentrated in knowledge intangibles, venture capital tilts–at both the sector and firm levels–toward organizational intangibles such as distribution, logistics, and payments. Highlighting the unique features of venture capital, this pattern is absent from public equity markets, where sectoral composition is far more similar across income levels. An accounting decomposition separates venture capital depth into the rate at which firms enter the market and the funding each entrant attracts, and entry accounts for the largest cross-country gaps. Moreover, the business environment is associated with VC primarily through entry, linked both to the size of the market and to the composition of what venture capital finances, the latter through entry into knowledge-intensive sectors in particular.

fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.title: Black Feminist Social Work: Centering Black Women's Knowledge in Social Work Theory, Education, Research, Policy, and Practice
fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.author: Talley, Vanessa M.
fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.summary: Social work acknowledges Black Feminist Thought as a framework and praxis, yet the profession has not established a social work framework that explicitly centers Black women’s epistemologies as foundational to education, theory, research, policy, and practice. Although social work maintains a historical commitment to social justice, person-in-environment, and human rights perspectives, dominant theories and knowledge systems continue to reflect Eurocentric assumptions regarding knowledge production and professional expertise. This article introduces Black Feminist Social Work (BFSW) as a conceptual framework that centers Black women’s individual and collective lived experiences, intellectual traditions, historical resistance, and knowledge to inform social work theory, education, research, policy, and practice. Drawing upon Black feminism, Black Feminist Thought, Womanism, Intersectionality, and the profession’s ethical commitments, the BFSW framework proposes a necessary shift from positioning Black women primarily as a population to be studied to recognizing them as producers of transformative knowledge. This article introduces four organizing principles, the Four C’s: Centering, Contextualizing, Co-Creating, and Changing, as foundational processes for Black Feminist Social Work and discusses the implications for curriculum development, clinical practice, research methodologies, policy advocacy, and future scholarship. Rather than positioning Black Feminist Social Work as an alternative specialization, this framework argues that centering Black women’s knowledge expands the social work profession’s capacity to pursue equity, liberation, and social transformation.

fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.title: Standardizing Business Process Documentation for Operational Transition: A Case Study of Employee Administration Data Entry at PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.author: Athira, Celia
fc066e842d:1ada7049cb8f2e03.summary: Organizational transitions that transfer operational activities from internal units to external partners depend heavily on the availability of standardized process documentation. This study examines the business process of Employee Administration (EA) Kedinasan data entry within the Employee & Organization Data Operation (EODO) unit of PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, undertaken as part of the company's preparation to transfer data-entry activities to an external partner, PT Infomedia Nusantara. Using a descriptive-qualitative case study approach grounded in Business Process Management (BPM) theory, the study maps the existing (as-is) process through direct observation, documentation review, and discussion with field supervisors, and evaluates it using SWOT analysis to identify internal and external factors shaping the transition. The findings show that although the EA Kedinasan process already possesses a structured workflow supported by verification and approval checkpoints and a centralized SAP-based system, its documentation remains fragmented across multiple work instructions and lacks an integrated reference that can function effectively as a knowledge-transfer medium for an external partner. The study recommends the consolidation of Business Process diagrams, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions, and a Playbook into a single coherent documentation package, which was implemented in part during the internship. Beyond its immediate organizational relevance, the case illustrates a broader tension in business process transitions: technically sound processes can still generate transition risk when explicit-knowledge artifacts are not consolidated for an external audience. The study contributes a practitioner-grounded account of how BPM and knowledge-transfer principles operate in a real outsourcing transition within a large Indonesian state-owned enterprise, and offers implications for organizations preparing similar administrative…
